newsitem.title: UK: Severn Trent aims for 10 pct buy back.
newsitem.headline: Severn Trent aims for 10 pct buy back.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Severn Trent Plc said on Tuesday it intended to buy back up to 10 percent of its shares "as soon as is appropriate."
It said in a statement accompanying its half year results that it would also seek to renew its mandate to buy back shares at the annual meeting in July 1997.

Severn Trent's pretax profits for the half year rise to 197 million pounds ($331.6 million) from 189 million pounds previously and it paid out a dividend of 10.5 pence, up from 9.2 pence, along with a second interim dividend of 3.84 pence.

The company said that the capital requirement for business growth was "relatively modest," which led it to make the share buyback, but added that it had also committed an extra 70 million pounds of new investment on water services.
Severn Trent had been expected to give some benefits to shareholders after its planned bid for sector fellow South West Water was blocked by the government earlier this year.

Severn Trent said its future direction was now clear in developing service and efficiency in water services, along with alliances with other utilities, and making its waste management company Biffa a leader in the UK.
